subject: Culture
title: Potlatch Ceremonies
description: A quick, practical guide to Potlatch Ceremonies.

hook.text: Pacific Northwest chiefs gained power by giving everything away—blankets, canoes, even copper shields.

buildup.text: The potlatch was a competitive feast where the host's status rose with each gift distributed to guests.

discovery.text: Some potlatches included deliberate destruction of property. Burning was proof you had more than you needed.

twist.text: Canada banned potlatch in 1884, calling it 'wasteful.' The real threat was a power system that didn't need money.

climax.text: The ban lasted until 1951. When it lifted, communities resumed potlatch within weeks. The tradition had survived.

punchline.text: Generosity as dominance confused every colonial accountant.

quiz.question: When did Canada ban the potlatch?
